title: Credential split by a separator that nothing removes
description: A credential is split by a line break that no surrounding construct removes: a literal line feed or carriage return plus line feed in plain text, a backslash-newline inside single quotes, a Markdown paragraph line ending.
semantics: The text holds two fragments and a separator that stays in the value, so the joined text is a different value from the original and is not the documented credential grammar. Whether the fragments are still a leak that must be protected, or are not a credential at all, is not settled by any source here: the outcome is left unresolved and the reading is recorded as inserts-separator, never rewritten by stripping whitespace.

applicability.rationale: Carrier-level: independent of the credential family.

evidenceBasis.rationale: The cited texts state that the separator is kept (single quotes preserve the literal value; a Markdown soft line break is treated like a space) but no source says what a consumer must do with such fragments. A maintainer decision with a non-author reviewer would settle it; candidate outcomes are protect the fragments (they are a partial leak) or leave them (the joined text is not a credential).

sources.supports: Enclosing characters in single-quotes shall preserve the literal value of each character within the single-quotes.
A soft line break is a line ending that is not a hard line break; it is treated like a space.

notes: Project-authored by the Redact Secret project, which maintains this repository; not independent evidence. Draft; not yet reviewed.
